evals.prompt: Architect the tenant onboarding orchestration layer using AWS Step Functions, DynamoDB, and SQS so buyer provisioning, entitlement fetches, and subscription webhook notifications are resilient to downstream transient failures.
evals.expected_output: Designs an idempotent **AWS Step Functions** onboarding workflow backed by a **`MarketplaceTenants` DynamoDB table** storing `{ CustomerIdentifier / LicenseArn, CustomerAWSAccountId, ProductCode, TenantId, SubscriptionStatus, EntitlementDimensions }` with a **Global Secondary Index (GSI) on `TenantId`** (enabling bidirectional lookup between AWS Marketplace identity and internal SaaS `TenantId`), plus **SQS queues with Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs)** subscribed to `aws-mp-subscription-notification` and `aws-mp-entitlement-notification`.
expectations: Activates the aws-marketplace-saas-architecture skill
Designs an idempotent Step Functions onboarding state machine persisting `MarketplaceTenants` in DynamoDB with a GSI on `TenantId`
Buffers `aws-mp-subscription-notification` and `aws-mp-entitlement-notification` SNS topics through SQS queues with DLQs

expectations: Activates the aws-marketplace-saas-architecture skill
Triggers hourly aggregation via EventBridge Scheduler (`rate(1 hour)`) and batches up to 25 records per `BatchMeterUsage` call
Persists `UsageRecordId`/`MeteringRecordId` and statuses (`Success`, `CustomerNotSubscribed`, `DuplicateRecord`) plus `UnprocessedRecords` retry handling

evals.prompt: We are shipping a Marketplace Paid Container product deployed by buyers onto either **Amazon EKS** or **Amazon ECS Fargate**. How should the container authenticate and call `RegisterUsage` / `MeterUsage`, and what common ECS role mistake causes `AccessDeniedException`?
evals.expected_output: Specifies short-lived workload IAM identities in the **buyer's running region** (never static IAM keys): (1) on **Amazon EKS**, bind a service account via **EKS Pod Identity** (`pods.eks.amazonaws.com` trust policy, or OIDC **IRSA**) granting `aws-marketplace:RegisterUsage` and `aws-marketplace:MeterUsage`; and (2) on **Amazon ECS Fargate**, attach `aws-marketplace:RegisterUsage` / `aws-marketplace:MeterUsage` to the **ECS Task Role (`TaskRoleArn`)** — flagging the classic mistake of attaching Marketplace permissions to the **ECS Task Execution Role (`ExecutionRoleArn`)**, which is only used by the ECS agent for ECR pulls and CloudWatch logs, not by application container code!
expectations: Activates the aws-marketplace-saas-architecture skill
Configures EKS Pod Identity (or IRSA) and ECS Task Roles granting `aws-marketplace:RegisterUsage` and `aws-marketplace:MeterUsage` in the cluster's region with zero static keys
Distinguishes `TaskRoleArn` (application container runtime identity) from `ExecutionRoleArn` (ECS agent image-pull/logging role)

evals.prompt: Why does our Lambda execution role get `AccessDeniedException` when calling `boto3.client('meteringmarketplace').resolve_customer(...)` and `boto3.client('marketplace-entitlement').get_entitlements(...)` even though our IAM policy grants `meteringmarketplace:ResolveCustomer`, `meteringmarketplace:BatchMeterUsage`, and `marketplace-entitlement:GetEntitlements`?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the AWS SDK client name vs IAM authorization prefix mismatch: although boto3 names the SDK clients `'meteringmarketplace'` and `'marketplace-entitlement'`, **all four IAM actions use the `aws-marketplace:` IAM service prefix** (`aws-marketplace:ResolveCustomer`, `aws-marketplace:BatchMeterUsage`, `aws-marketplace:MeterUsage`, `aws-marketplace:GetEntitlements`) on `Resource: "*"`. Provides the corrected least-privilege JSON IAM policy.
expectations: Activates the aws-marketplace-saas-architecture skill
Identifies that `meteringmarketplace:*` and `marketplace-entitlement:*` are boto3 client names, whereas IAM authorization requires the `aws-marketplace:` action prefix
Outputs the corrected least-privilege IAM policy with `aws-marketplace:ResolveCustomer`, `aws-marketplace:BatchMeterUsage`, `aws-marketplace:MeterUsage`, and `aws-marketplace:GetEntitlements`

evals.prompt: Our SaaS API receives `8,000` requests/second across 500 Marketplace tenants. If our auth authorizer calls `marketplace-entitlement:GetEntitlements` on every HTTP request to check seat limits and subscription status, what breaks and how should we architect it instead?
evals.expected_output: Warns that calling `marketplace-entitlement:GetEntitlements` (`us-east-1`) synchronously on every `8,000 req/s` API call will immediately hit severe **AWS API throttling (`ThrottlingException`)** and add cross-region network latency to every request. Instead, store authoritative `{ TenantId, SubscriptionStatus, EntitlementDimensions }` in **`MarketplaceTenants` DynamoDB** (with `TenantId` GSI + in-memory/ElastiCache short-TTL cache in the authorizer), and update/invalidate cache asynchronously only when `aws-mp-entitlement-notification` or `aws-mp-subscription-notification` events arrive via SQS.
expectations: Activates the aws-marketplace-saas-architecture skill
Explains that per-request `GetEntitlements` calls at `8,000 req/s` cause severe throttling and cross-region latency
Architects local DynamoDB (`MarketplaceTenants` `TenantId` GSI) + authorizer/ElastiCache caching invalidated asynchronously by SQS-buffered Marketplace SNS events
